title: In Psalms 21 What Does This Psalm Teach Us About The Relationship Between The King And God
paragraphs: The Relationship Between the King and God in Psalm 21: A Bible Study

Psalm 21 is a royal psalm attributed to David, focusing on the king’s victory and the blessings he receives from God. It is a song of thanksgiving and praise, celebrating how God answers the prayers of the king and establishes his reign. This psalm provides profound insight into the relationship between the king and God, revealing spiritual principles relevant for all who seek to understand God's sovereignty and the nature of godly leadership.
1. The King’s Dependence on God
The psalm opens by highlighting the king’s joy and strength—not in his own power, but in the Lord:
The king shall joy in thy strength, O Jehovah; And in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice! - Psalm 21:1 ASV

This verse teaches that the king’s victories and successes are rooted in God’s strength and salvation. The king is not self-sufficient; his achievements come from the Lord. This reinforces the biblical principle that true leadership begins with humility and reliance on God (Proverbs 3:5-6 ASV).
2. God’s Generous Blessings
God is depicted as the giver of every good thing the king enjoys:
Thou hast given him his heart’s desire, And hast not withholden the request of his lips. - Psalm 21:2 ASV

This relationship is marked by answered prayer and divine favor. The king’s desires are aligned with God’s will, and God responds graciously. This echoes the promise that those who delight in the Lord will receive the desires of their heart (Psalm 37:4 ASV).
3. The Gift of Life and Honor
God blesses the king with life, honor, and enduring blessings:
He asked life of thee, thou gavest it him, Even length of days for ever and ever. His glory is great in thy salvation: Honor and majesty dost thou lay upon him. - Psalm 21:4-5 ASV

These verses reflect that the king’s life and reign are gifts from God. In a broader, prophetic sense, these blessings find their ultimate fulfillment in Christ—the eternal King—who receives glory, honor, and everlasting life (Philippians 2:9-11 ASV).
4. The Security and Confidence Found in God
The king’s confidence is not in his own ability, but in God’s steadfast love and faithfulness:
For the king trusteth in Jehovah; And through the lovingkindness of the Most High he shall not be moved. - Psalm 21:7 ASV

This trust forms the foundation for stability and unshakeable leadership. The king’s faith in God’s covenant love ensures that he will stand firm even in adversity. This principle applies to all believers: our security is found in God’s faithfulness, not our own strength (Psalm 125:1 ASV).
5. God’s Judgment on the King’s Enemies
The latter part of the psalm describes God’s active role in protecting the king and judging his enemies:
Thy hand will find out all thine enemies; Thy right hand will find out those that hate thee. - Psalm 21:8 ASV

This demonstrates that the king’s authority and security are ultimately upheld by God’s justice. The king does not take vengeance into his own hands but trusts in God’s righteous judgment. This foreshadows the ultimate victory of Christ over all evil (Revelation 19:11-16 ASV).
6. The Call to Praise
The psalm ends with a call to praise God for his power and faithfulness:
Be thou exalted, O Jehovah, in thy strength: So will we sing and praise thy power. - Psalm 21:13 ASV
Worship and thanksgiving are the natural response to God’s work on behalf of his king. God’s people are invited to join in this praise, acknowledging that every victory and blessing comes from Him.
Conclusion: Lessons for Today

Psalm 21 teaches us that the relationship between the king and God is one of dependence, trust, and covenant love. The king’s victories, blessings, and security all originate from God’s hand. This points ultimately to Jesus Christ, the true King, whose reign is eternal and whose victory is complete. For believers today, it is a reminder to trust in God’s provision, rejoice in His salvation, and praise Him for His faithfulness.
